sources.title: Configure permissions: permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model; approval table: read-only (file reads, Grep) no, Bash commands yes except a built-in set of read-only commands, file modification yes; to inspect the full command text with your own logic before it runs, use a PreToolUse hook; PreToolUse hook decisions don't bypass permission rules

layout.description: Real run, recorded on Nov 2, 2026 with Claude Code 2.1.309 (model claude-haiku-5-5). Three runs without any approval, every run twice: reading with Read worked. Creating a file with Write did not. Starting a script with Bash did not, two attempts were blocked, and Claude read the source instead. That matches the table in the docs.
layout.companion_text: Base command per run: claude -p "<Prompt>" --model haiku --output-format stream-json --verbose --setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --tools Read,Write,Bash. All runs with --tools Read,Write,Bash, without --allowedTools and without --permission-mode (default). The script zeige.js creates lief.txt when it runs; that is how the run checks whether it ran. Source: Claude Code docs, Permissions, retrieved Nov 2, 2026. Paths shortened in the frame (test folder = .). Behaviour can change with version and model. Not an official Anthropic channel.

beats.spoken: Which tools can Claude Code use without your approval? Three real runs without any consent at all: read a file, write a file, start a script.
The test folder holds a note and a small script. When the script runs, it writes a file called lief.txt. That way you can see whether it really ran, and not just what Claude says about it.
Run one, read. Claude read notiz.txt with the Read tool and named the first line. No question, no block, done in under twenty seconds.
Run two, write. Claude tried to create gruss.txt with the Write tool. Writing had not been approved, the file never appeared, and Claude said it had not tried another way around the gate.

Run three, start a script. The first Bash command needed approval. Claude read the script, called it harmless and tried again as a single command. That was blocked too, and Claude stopped. lief.txt never appeared.
All three runs ran twice, with the same result. Reading worked without approval, writing and Bash did not. That is exactly what the table in the docs says.

data.headline: 3 runs, twice each
data.note: Reading: no approval. Bash, file edits: approval (per the docs).

beats.spoken: So Claude may read right away. For writing and commands, you need an approval or a rule. Follow Promptwerk for more Claude workflows, step by step.

data.statement: Read right away, write and run with approval.
